Gyüre Jewish Cemetery One

Jewish Cemetery · Gyüre, Hungary

Not demolished. Gyüre's Jewish cemetery, in use from 1819 to at least 1944, served a community that peaked at 151 residents in 1870. The village had just two Jewish residents in the 1770s; after losing independent status to the Kisvárda community in 1880, Rabbi Samuel Roth reorganized and broke Gyüre's Jewish community away from Kisvárda again in 1925, building a mikveh, synagogue, and shochet despite its small size. The community endured disturbances from Romanian soldiers around World War I and later anti-Jewish violence from the Rongyos Gárda paramilitary following the Treaty of Trianon. In spring 1944, German and Hungarian authorities deported all 98 of Gyüre's Jews to the Kisvárda Ghetto, then to Auschwitz on May 25.
